---
title: "Making decisions at the speed of the team"
description: "Most decisions are two-way doors. Treat them that way and your team moves faster, and learns more."
date: 2026-09-21
categories: [Leadership, decisions]

---

The slowest teams I've worked with weren't short on talent. They were short on
**permission**. Every choice waited for the one person who could make it.

## Sort the door first

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  Q[A decision lands on your desk] --> R{Easy to reverse?}
  R -->|Yes: two-way door| S[Decide in the room.<br/>Tell people after.]
  R -->|No: one-way door| T[Write it down.<br/>Get two other views.]
  T --> U[Decide within a week]
  S --> V[Review in a month]
  U --> V
```

## Three habits that help

1. **Name the door.** Say out loud whether this is reversible. It changes the energy in the room.
2. **Set a decision date.** Open-ended discussions expand to fill the calendar.
3. **Write the "why" in two sentences.** Future you will thank present you.

> Speed comes from trust, and trust comes from seeing decisions explained.

::: {.callout-important}
## The trap
"Let's take this offline" is often a one-way door in disguise. Agree who decides, and by when, before anyone leaves.
:::
